instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, add it to a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until the pork is ready.
Cut the pork across the grain into thin rounds, about 1/4 inch thick. Transfer it to a bowl, toss with the salt and let it sit while you make the dressing.
Make the dressing in a large bowl. Mince the garlic and 1 of the chilies (seeds out), then add the juice of 2 limes (about 1/4 cup), the fish sauce and the sugar. Stir until the sugar dissolves.
Cut half the head of cabbage into fine shreds and spread them on a platter. Slice the second chili thin, with the seeds, and set it in a small bowl for the table. Chop 2 tbsp of the cilantro.
Put the pork in a large skillet with 1/3 cup water and set it over medium-high heat. Spread it out and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the slices are opaque all the way through.
You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick slice there. No thermometer? Cut one slice open. It's done when there's no pink left.
Drain the pork in a sieve over a bowl. Stir 2 tbsp of the cooking liquid into the dressing.
Add the warm pork to the dressing and toss until every slice is coated. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lime.
Spoon the pork and dressing over the cabbage and scatter the cilantro on top. Serve with the rice and the bowl of sliced chili for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: Hungry in Thailand leads: a pan-poached sliced tenderloin tossed in a raw garlic, chili, fish sauce, sugar and lime dressing over shredded cabbage. Taste of Siam steams the pork and stirs a spoon of the pork liquid into the sauce, which this version borrows. Both are fiery, so the chili in the base is cut to half a seeded Fresno and the rest goes in a bowl for the table. The listed 30 minute rest was dropped; the pork is salted while the dressing is made. No source had 20 ratings.
